movingSpeed.purpose: A tracked object whose Kalman-estimated centre speed exceeds this is 'moving'.
movingSpeed.ref: Placeholder until measured; see docs/COMPUTER_VISION_RESEARCH.md (tracker noise on static scenes).

stillSpeed.purpose: Below this speed an object is 'static' (hysteresis band between stillSpeed and movingSpeed keeps the previous state).

reversalWindowMs.purpose: Window in which horizontal direction reversals of a moving object are counted (repeated-movement observation).
reversalWindowMs.ref: Covers a few back-and-forth hand movements.

persistentAfterMs.purpose: A confirmed track visible for this long counts as a persistent object in the scene model.
persistentAfterMs.ref: Three times the track loss buffer: excludes objects passing through the view.

occludedFraction.purpose: An object whose box is covered at least this much by other objects' boxes (or cut by the frame edge) is flagged as occluded.
occludedFraction.ref: Box overlap is a proxy: without depth or masks the front/back order is unknown, so the flag means 'partly hidden or overlapping'.

threshold.purpose: Fingerprint distance to the last analysed frame above which the scene counts as changed (new view).
threshold.ref: Measured with the fake-camera feed in headless Chromium: frames of the same scene 0.00-0.09, cuts between photos 0.85-0.87. 0.32 leaves margin for hand-held drift (not measured on a real phone).

settleMotion.purpose: Frames with motion below this are 'settled' and preferred for analysis.
settleMotion.ref: Measured with the fake-camera feed: static scenes give motion 0.00-0.04; 0.07 sits above that noise.

maxSettleWaitMs.purpose: Maximum wait for a settled frame before analysing anyway.
maxSettleWaitMs.ref: Longer than the track loss buffer (1000 ms) so coasting tracks expire first.

intervalMs.purpose: How often the live scene model is sent to the local diagnostic engine when it has changed.
intervalMs.ref: Fast enough to confirm a finding within ~3 s (two observations), small JSON payloads only.

heartbeatMs.purpose: Maximum time between observations even when nothing changed, so time-based rules and resolutions progress.
heartbeatMs.ref: Bounds how long a resolved issue can stay displayed as open.

confirmObservations.purpose: A local finding becomes CONFIRMED after being observed this many times...
confirmObservations.ref: Temporal confirmation instead of single-frame evidence (cf. ByteTrack confirming tracks on the second detection).

confirmMinSpanMs.ref: One observation interval: rules out a single noisy frame.

trackingObservations.purpose: Observations after which a confirmed finding is TRACKING.
trackingObservations.ref: Matches the previous AI-only lifecycle (third sighting).

resolveAfterMs.purpose: A local finding is RESOLVED when its rule has not fired for this long while the camera still looks at the same scene...
resolveAfterMs.ref: Three times the track loss buffer; avoids flapping on a brief detection drop.

resolveObservations.purpose: ...and over at least this many consecutive observations.
resolveObservations.ref: Hysteresis: one empty observation never resolves a finding.

exitEdgeMargin.purpose: When an object involved in a finding is no longer tracked and its last box was within this distance of the frame edge, it is assumed to have left the view: the finding becomes NOT VISIBLE instead of counting towards resolution.
exitEdgeMargin.ref: Objects leave the view across an edge; an object that vanishes from the middle of an unchanged view was moved or removed.

sampleIntervalS.purpose: Target spacing of sampled video frames.
sampleIntervalS.ref: Two samples per second captures object entries/exits in handheld clips.

minSamples.purpose: Lower bound on samples for very short clips.
minSamples.ref: Enough to find at least one scene boundary.

maxSamples.purpose: Upper bound on samples (cost cap for long videos).
maxSamples.ref: Keeps on-device processing under ~15 s on a laptop.

sceneBoundary.purpose: Fingerprint distance between consecutive samples that starts a new scene.
sceneBoundary.ref: Histogram-difference shot-boundary detection; tuned on test clips.

sceneDrift.purpose: Distance from a scene's first sample that starts a new scene (catches slow pans).

dedupe.purpose: Samples closer than this to the previous kept sample of the same scene are redundant.
dedupe.ref: Below compression noise between consecutive frames of a still shot.

maxKeyframes.ref: Deep detection and optional AI reasoning only see keyframes.

representativeWindow.purpose: Representative frame chosen from this part of each scene (avoids transitions).
representativeWindow.ref: Scene starts/ends often contain motion blur from the cut or pan.
